purpose: Prevent agents and operators from invoking post-setup fleet launchers before bootstrap/readiness state has been proved, and route setup, readiness, sprint launch, validation, artifacts, and handoff through repository-owned surfaces.

directories.purpose: Repository-owned setup, readiness, GNHF sprint, fleet, and status implementations.
Lifecycle map, workflows, registry, fixtures, report, and opt-in hook for fleet bootstrap and task launch readiness.
Scoped procedure for deciding whether to bootstrap, list readiness, authenticate interactively, or launch a bounded sprint.
Human-readable fleet readiness and failure-recovery guide.
Windows/Linux exact-head validation for the harness.

knownTraps: Do not invoke %LOCALAPPDATA%\AgentSwitchboard\GnhfFleet\agent-switchboard.cmd until both the installed launcher and state.json have been checked. A missing launcher is a bootstrap/readiness-state failure, not an agent failure.
A successful tmux/WezTerm/WSL proof does not prove the GNHF fleet is installed. Terminal readiness and agent-fleet readiness are separate gates.
If state.json is missing, run the repository-owned setup/bootstrap workflow before listing agents or launching a sprint.
If exactly one of state.json or agent-switchboard.cmd exists, classify the installation as inconsistent/partial and run setup in repair mode; do not synthesize or copy the missing file manually.
Adapter READY does not prove provider authentication, exact model availability, quota, or hosted response. Preserve launch-time provider probes and interactive authentication boundaries.
For non-AgentSwitchboard target repositories, always supply -Prompt or -PromptPath; bundled default prompts are intentionally scoped to AgentSwitchboard only.
The target repository must satisfy the GNHF clean-checkout contract before sprint launch. Preserve unrelated dirty work rather than stashing, resetting, or overwriting it.
Push is off by default. A local bounded sprint commit is not merged, deployed, or provider-accepted proof.
Setup and readiness artifacts belong under the registered local paths and must not be committed to the repository.
A post-setup command shown before setup state is proved is an operator-command sequencing defect even if the command would be correct after bootstrap.
proofCeiling: Tracked lifecycle contracts can prove deterministic bootstrap/readiness routing, artifact ownership, command ordering, and CI validation. They do not prove that a particular workstation is bootstrapped, authenticated, provider-responsive, or capable of completing a repository sprint until corresponding runtime evidence is observed.
